findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the customer master spreadsheet uploaded to it) are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

No ACL, public access block, or bucket policy restricting access is configured, and the inline comment states the bucket is public; the bucket holds a customer master file, so public exposure would leak sensitive data.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to a bucket containing sensitive customer data is not auditable, hindering detection of unauthorised access.
Versioning is disabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be permanently deleted or overwritten (including by an attacker) with no recovery path or MFA delete protection.
There is no bucket policy denying non-HTTPS requests (aws:SecureTransport false), allowing data to be transmitted to and from the bucket in cleartext.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data in unencrypted public bucket
findings.description: A file named customer-master.xlsx is uploaded with no kms_key_id or server-side encryption specified into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is unencrypted and publicly accessible, exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
Although the ACL is private, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could inadvertently expose financial data publicly.
No logging block is configured for a bucket holding financial data, so access to it cannot be audited.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, allowing irreversible deletion or overwriting of financial records with no recovery or MFA delete safeguard.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so financial data may be transferred over unencrypted HTTP.

The operations bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 default encryption. Any data written there is unprotected at rest by customer-controlled keys.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so object-level and bucket access requests are not recorded to the logs bucket, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access.
The bucket relies solely on a private ACL with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so a later public ACL or bucket policy could expose its contents without any account-level guardrail.
The data_science bucket declares no default server-side encryption, so potentially sensitive analytics datasets are stored unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, leaving no defence-in-depth control against a future public ACL or policy granting anonymous read access.

The central log bucket has no public access block; because it uses the log-delivery-write ACL and aggregates audit data, accidental public exposure would leak access records for the whole environment.
The log aggregation bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or reading of stored audit logs is not recorded.
None of these buckets attach a policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so data can be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
